Middleware

Middleware allows you to run code before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly. This is useful for handling things like authentication, A/B testing, redirects, and more advanced server-side logic that you want to run before reaching your route handlers.

Convention

Use the file middleware.ts (or .js) in the root of your project to define Middleware. For example, at the same level as pages or app, or inside src if applicable. Next.js will automatically detect and load the file at build time.

Using JWT

For authentication flows, you can verify a JWT inside the Middleware before the request reaches your route handlers. When the token is missing or invalid, return a redirect response to your login page so that protected routes never serve unauthenticated traffic.

Matching paths

The optional matcher config lets Middleware run only on matching paths. You can supply a single path, an array of paths, or use regex-like syntax. This avoids invoking Middleware for every request and keeps cold-start overhead low.

Examples

  • Single path: matcher: '/about/:path*'
  • Multiple paths: matcher: ['/about/:path*', '/dashboard/:path*']
